title: Licensure of non-resident pharmacies that dispense or ship into Massachusetts
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39J(a) directs the Board to establish a procedure to license non-resident pharmacies, which prescribe, ship, mail, sell or dispense medications in the commonwealth; s. 39D defines a non-resident pharmacy as any pharmacy located outside the commonwealth that prescribes, ships, mails, sells or dispenses medications in the commonwealth. Under s. 39J(b) a non-resident pharmacy shall designate a pharmacist in charge who shall register with the Board, shall be responsible for the pharmacy's compliance with chapter 112, and shall be licensed and in good standing with the board of pharmacy of the state in which the pharmacy is located; the pharmacist in charge discloses the location, name and title of all principal managers and a letter of good standing from the in-state board, and submits that report annually and within 30 days after any change of office, corporate office or manager of record; certifies that the pharmacy maintains at all times a current unrestricted license, permit or registration in its home jurisdiction and maintains records of all drugs dispensed to patients in the commonwealth readily available on the Board's request; the pharmacy notifies the Board of any enforcement or disciplinary action taken against it in any state; and a list of drugs dispensed in the commonwealth is sent to the Board annually. Under s. 39J(c) no pharmacy or pharmacist operating outside the state shall prescribe, ship, mail, sell, transfer or dispense drug preparations in the commonwealth unless they are produced in a pharmacy granted a non-resident license under s. 39J. Under s. 39J(e) a non-resident licence holder is subject to the prescription monitoring requirements of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A and is not eligible for a waiver under that section; an application shall not be approved unless the applicant demonstrates the ability to comply with s. 24A, and the Board may revoke the licence for failure to comply. Under 247 CMR 6.02(4) a pharmacy located outside Massachusetts may not dispense or ship any controlled substance into Massachusetts unless it holds a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license. Under 247 CMR 6.09(1) the applicant submits the documentation in 247 CMR 6.04(2), proof of good standing from the state where the pharmacy is located dated within three months of the application submission date, and an inspection report from a Board approved inspector conducted within two years of the application submission date; the Board may require an additional inspection before final approval, by an agent of the Board or a Board approved inspector, with all costs of third party inspectors paid by the applicant; a pharmacy seeking to dispense or ship any controlled substance into Massachusetts shall have a designated Massachusetts licensed pharmacist in charge; the licence expires on December 31st of each odd numbered year following issuance; and on renewal the licensee submits copies of all reports or correspondence pertaining to all inspections by any state or federal agency, or any entity inspecting on its behalf, occurring within the pending licensing period. Under 247 CMR 6.09(4) a non-resident pharmacy shall apply to the Board for approval whenever there is a change of its Massachusetts licensed designated pharmacist in charge, within 90 days of the termination or resignation of the previous pharmacist in charge.
exam_relevance: Tests that Massachusetts licenses out-of-state pharmacies that ship in, that the licence runs on the Drug Store odd-year cycle, and the separate 30-day, three-month, two-year and 90-day periods attached to it.

exceptions: A non-resident pharmacy is not eligible for a waiver under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 24A.
common_confusions: The non-resident pharmacist in charge must be licensed in the home state; 247 CMR 6.09(1)(c) separately requires a designated Massachusetts licensed pharmacist in charge for a pharmacy dispensing or shipping controlled substances into Massachusetts.
The 30-day statutory report and the 90-day regulatory application are different duties counted from different events.
Compounded sterile and complex non-sterile preparations need an additional non-resident compounding licence.
